title: Add or subtract decimals to hundredths

beats.say: Find zero point eight plus nine point two six.
Estimate first. Zero point eight is almost one, so the sum is about one plus nine: about ten.
Stack them so the points line up, not the last digits.
Then every place lines up: ones over ones, tenths over tenths, hundredths over hundredths.
Zero point eight has no hundredths, so write a zero there. A zero on the end changes nothing: still eight tenths.
Now add from the right, just like whole numbers. Hundredths: zero plus six is six.
Tenths: eight plus two is ten tenths, and ten tenths make one whole. Write zero, carry the one to the ones.
Ones: one plus zero plus nine is ten. That is one ten and zero ones.
The point comes straight down: ten point zero six.
That is about ten, as the estimate said.
Find twelve point zero six minus two point two five.
Stack them, points lined up, the larger number on top.
Subtract from the right. Hundredths: six minus five is one.
Tenths: zero minus two? Trade one of the two ones for ten tenths. Ten minus two is eight.
Ones: one minus two? Trade the ten for ten more ones: eleven ones. Eleven minus two is nine.
Nothing is left in the tens. Nine point eight one.
Check by adding back: nine point eight one plus two point two five is twelve point zero six.
Adding and subtracting decimals always goes the same way.
One: line up the points, not the last digits.

beats.say: Two: fill in zeros on the end. They change nothing.

beats.say: Three: then it is whole numbers. Work from the right, carrying and trading as always.
